YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178#2/r2.claim: A future intention must be qualified by God's will; when the Prophet promised to answer the Jews the next day without qualifying it, the verse was revealed, and remembering later requires saying 'if God wills'.

FARRA:v2p138/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p138/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p138/r2.claim: إلا أن يشاء الله means to say إن شاء الله; the omitted sense is not to promise tomorrow except with God's will.

NAHHAS:v2p453/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p453/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p453/r1.claim: Ghadan is a time adverb, originally ghuduw.

SULAMI:v1p408#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p408#3/r1.claim: The Prophet could speak about God only as God informed him and could promise his own action only subject to his Lord's will.

THALABI:v6p163/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p163/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p163/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when resolved to do something or swear about tomorrow, one should add 'if God wills'; if forgotten, say it when remembered even after a year.

THALABI:v6p163/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p163/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p163/r2.claim: The instruction corrects the Prophet's promise to answer questions about the cave youths, the Spirit, and Dhul-Qarnayn without making an exception.

THALABI:v6p163/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p163/r3.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v6p163/r3.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says a servant's faith is incomplete until he qualifies all his speech with an exception.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r1.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r1.claim: The exception has an ellipsis: do not say it unless you say, if God wills.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r2.claim: This is guidance to attach God's will to a decision rather than make an unconditional commitment, since an obstacle might prevent it and turn the promise into a lie; Moses was not lying when he failed to be patient because he qualified his promise.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r3.claim: Mentioning God's will acknowledges that He governs actions through His power and assistance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p298/r4.claim: For an oath, adding إن شاء الله can remove the need for expiation if the oath is broken.

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r4.claim: Since events issue from God's will, one who knows God cannot promise future action as if it were completed by oneself.

QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p216/r5.claim: A believer resolves to obey while inwardly disclaiming personal power and witnessing what unfolds through divine decree.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r1.claim: The command disciplines the Prophet to qualify a future resolve with God's will: say “if God wills” when promising to do something tomorrow.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r3.claim: The particle “an” is accusative: do not say you will act except by God's will; he supplies an implied preposition.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r4.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, understand an omitted “say”: “unless he says, if God wills”; a short expression can stand for the longer one by indication.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r5.speaker: المبرد عن الكسائي والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p581#2/r5.claim: They likewise supply an omitted verb of saying; deleting it shifts “wills” into the future form.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:23-25/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:23-25/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:23-25/r1.claim: God disciplines the Prophet to add “if God wills” when he resolves to do something tomorrow.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r1.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r1.claim: One view ties the command to the Prophet's promise to answer the questioners the next day without saying ‘if God wills.’

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r2.claim: The author prefers a general rule for everyone to attach an exception to future plans, avoiding false promises or broken commitments.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r3.claim: He rejects restricting the verse to the Prophet's incident: the Prophet only spoke with revelation and permission, so an authorized prediction would not fail and a failed promise would repel people.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r4.claim: An exception is required for possible future events, not certainties; the promise of entering the Sacred Mosque was conditional because some might die first.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r5.claim: When resolving to do something tomorrow, say that you will do it if God wills.

JISHUMI:v6p4390/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4390/r6.claim: The address is understood either as directed to the Prophet alone or, preferably, to him and his community.

JISHUMI:v6p4395/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4395/r2.claim: Calling a future act ‘a thing’ shows that a nonexistent thing can still be called a thing, against those who reserve the term for existing things.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.claim: One should not promise to act tomorrow without adding God's will; after promising answers to Meccan questions the next day without this phrase, revelation paused for days.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p668#2/r1.claim: “For a thing” means concerning something one resolves to do; “tomorrow” means any future time, not only the next day.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r10.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:18:22-24/r10.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi explains the rule by the risk that a person may be prevented by illness, incapacity, or a change of intention; saying ‘if God wills’ avoids a false report because the act did not occur only if God did not will it.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r6.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:18:22-24/r6.claim: One reading of the exception supplies an implied verb: do not promise tomorrow unless you say ‘if God wills’; this teaches people to qualify future promises and avoid a lie or broken oath if prevented.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:22-24/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas associates the exception with teaching people to qualify what they report they will do, so an obstacle does not make the report false or an oath broken.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r8.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:18:22-24/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ reads the exception literally as ‘only by God's will’; this fits the surface wording without supplying omitted speech, and can mean that one should promise only acts God wills, namely obedience.

TABRISI:18:22-24/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:22-24/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:22-24/r9.claim: On al-Farraʾ's reading, the exception does not bar reports about permissible acts, since the prohibition is discouragement rather than a ban: omitting it is not sinful by consensus.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r1.claim: Quraysh asked the Prophet about Dhul-Qarnayn, the Spirit, and the Companions of the Cave; he promised an answer tomorrow without saying God willing, so Gabriel's revelation was delayed fifteen days and he was distressed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p127#2/r2.claim: The exception means one must say that the action will happen if God wills; the verb saying is omitted.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:23-24/r2.claim: One should not state a future intention as certain without attaching it to God's will; otherwise failure to do it makes the assertion a lie. The lām in li-shayʾ means 'concerning' or 'for'.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p10#2/r1.claim: The prohibition concerns any thing one intends to do in the future; “tomorrow” means the future generally, not only the next day.

QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r1.claim: God teaches the Prophet proper courtesy after forbidding disputation: speak of a future act only when God permits or while explicitly attaching it to His will.

QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:23-24/r2.claim: People should ascribe action to God’s will rather than their own, since they act through Him and His willing.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r3.claim: The Prophet said he would answer the next day without saying if God wills; revelation paused fifteen days, prompting Meccan rumors that his jinn inspiration had left him, then came with the answers and more.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r10.claim: Reports say revelation was delayed fifteen days or forty days after the Prophet’s promise without qualification.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p161#2/r9.claim: The Prophet must not promise a future act without tying it to God’s will; the reported occasion is his answer to Quraysh that he would tell them tomorrow about the cave, al-Khiḍr, and the Spirit, without saying in shāʾ Allāh.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r1.claim: When resolving to do something later, the Messenger is taught to make it conditional on God's will: God knows the unseen, what occurred and will occur, and even what would have happened had it not happened.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r2.claim: The Prophet reports that Solomon vowed to visit seventy women that night, with narrations giving ninety or one hundred; an angel told him to say God willing, but he did not, and only one woman bore half a person.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r3.claim: The Prophet said that had Solomon said God willing, he would not have broken his oath and would have attained his wish, with all sons becoming horsemen for God's cause.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p148/r4.claim: The passage was also revealed after the Prophet promised to answer a question about the Sleepers the next day; revelation was delayed fifteen days, as recounted earlier in the sura.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p149/r5.claim: Two al-Tabarani reports explain the instruction as remembering to say God willing: one comes through Jabir ibn Zayd and one through Mujahid.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r5.claim: A person should not state a resolved plan for tomorrow, trivial or important, without connecting it to God's will and acknowledging dependence on Him.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p460/r6.claim: A promise made without saying God willing may fail through an obstacle and become falsehood that repels listeners.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r1.claim: After Quraysh asked about the sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit on Jewish advice, the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying إن شاء الله; Gabriel was delayed fifteen days, then explained the omission and brought the answers.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r10.claim: The Dajjal's forty days include one like a year, one like a month, one like a week, and a final day like an ordinary day.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r2.claim: Gabriel explained that his delay followed the Prophet's failure to qualify his promise with God's will.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r4.claim: When the answer matched what the Jews had said about the third question, Quraysh called the two revelations cooperating sorceries, meaning the Torah and Quran, and rejected both.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r5.claim: The Prophet warned that every prophet warned his people about the Dajjal; he would certainly emerge among this final community, and God would be each Muslim's protector.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r6.claim: The Dajjal will emerge between Iraq and Syria and devastate lands to either side; he will claim prophethood while denying that any prophet follows Muhammad.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r7.claim: The word كافر will appear between the Dajjal's eyes and every believer will read it; believers are instructed to recite the opening passages of al-Kahf against him.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r8.claim: The Dajjal will kill one person and revive him, but will not be able to exercise that power over another person.

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r9.claim: The Dajjal's apparent paradise is fire and his fire is paradise; a believer tested by the fire should close his eyes and seek God's help, and it will be cool and safe like the fire for Abraham.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r1.claim: On Jewish advice Quraysh asked the Prophet about the Cave sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; he promised to answer the next day without an exception, and Gabriel did not come until God willed.

DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p377/r2.claim: The Prophet explained that the delay distressed him because he had no knowledge of the answers before revelation; a puppy in his house was also why Gabriel did not enter.

BURSEVI:v5p180#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180#2/r1.speaker: الخضر
BURSEVI:v5p180#2/r1.claim: He lists ranks of saints and says they attained them through truthful scrupulousness, pure intention, sound hearts, and mercy toward Muslims rather than abundant worship or outward adornment. They curse no one, harm or belittle those below them, envy no one above them, and are generous, gentle, and pleasant.

BURSEVI:v5p180#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p180#2/r2.claim: In the inward allegory, the company represents the spirit, heart, innate and acquired intellect, sacred power, and the secret faculties in the body's cave; Decianus is the commanding ego.

BURSEVI:v5p180#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p180#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p180#2/r3.claim: The verse teaches etiquette in future commitments; it followed the Jews' instructions to Quraysh to ask about the Spirit, the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn. Muhammad promised an answer the next day without saying إن شاء الله; revelation paused, and Quraysh said his Lord had abandoned him.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#2/r1.claim: The prohibition covers promising to do anything one resolves in the future; ghadan primarily means the next day but the active participle already conveys futurity, which the phrase reinforces.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#2/r2.claim: The occasion was Quraysh asking the Prophet about the Spirit, the Companions of the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn; he said he would answer the next day without qualifying the promise, and revelation was delayed fifteen days, with other reports giving three or forty.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p247#2/r3.claim: Some limit the wording to the literal next day and derive broader future promises by implication; Alusi rejects the objection that later periods differ because obstacles can fade, since death is an obstacle and its possibility increases over time.

ELMALILI:18:23/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:23/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:23/r1.claim: Human resolve alone cannot bring an event about, so plans for the future must be tied to God's will; a person does not know what tomorrow will bring.

TABATABAI:18:23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:23/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:23/r1.claim: A report says Jews suggested three questions to Quraysh as a test of prophethood: the cave companions, Moses and his youth, and Dhul-Qarnayn.

TABATABAI:18:23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:23/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:23/r2.claim: Unlike the Dhul-Qarnayn account, the cave story does not begin with an explicit question formula, though the closing command about tomorrow hints at the question.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r3.claim: The instruction applies to anyone who plans and announces a future action; all beings, acts, and effects belong to God, who may determine them without challenge.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#21/r4.claim: Causes and agents have no independent efficacy: God empowers them and permits their effects, or withholds power by willing otherwise.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#22/r1.claim: The Quran repeatedly says that human acts and natural processes occur by God's permission, including cutting trees, calamities, plant growth, death, faith, and a messenger’s obedience.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#22/r2.claim: A believer should recognize that God grants ownership and power, rely on Him when resolving to act, and qualify future promises by God's permission or lack of contrary will.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#22/r3.claim: The verse does not forbid attributing actions to people, which the Quran often does; its exception corrects the claim that people act independently of God's will and permission.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r1.claim: The exception modifies the circumstances or times of the statement: say you will act tomorrow only while attaching God’s will, meaning permission for the action.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r2.speaker: الأخفش
TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash reads an omitted verb say in the exception, making this etiquette that avoids falsehood or broken promises if prevented; the author rejects it as needless strain that changes the meaning.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r3.claim: Some exegetes read the phrase as an object of divine will, restricting it to obedient acts; the author rejects this legislative reading as unsupported.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#23/r4.claim: The legislative interpretation lacks evidence: God’s will is not used this way in the Quran, which does use exceptions of creative will.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r1.claim: Another Muʿtazili interpretation makes the exception modify the act rather than the statement, with God preventing an independently caused act; the author rejects it because Quranic usage accepts that construction.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r2.claim: A proposal that God must first authorize disclosure of what He has informed the Prophet requires an unsupported implied object and otherwise imposes an unknowable duty.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r3.claim: A final proposal treats the exception as eternal, meaning never state a future intention; this conflicts with Quranic passages attributing future actions to the Prophet and others.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#24/r4.claim: The Quran itself presents Moses, Shuʿayb, Ishmael, and the Prophet as speaking of future acts conditionally on God’s will, supporting the ordinary permission reading.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:9-26#27/r1.claim: The Prophet promised answers the next day without saying if God wills; revelation stopped for forty days, causing grief and doubt while Quraysh mocked, then Gabriel explained revelation comes only by God’s permission.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r8.claim: An account from ʿAlī says a person swearing by God may make an exception for forty days, recalling the Prophet’s delayed answer to Jewish questioners after he omitted “if God wills.”

TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī defines thunyā as an exception and says related reports suggest a decisive oath; whether an exception can qualify an already binding oath is left to jurisprudence.

ASAD-NOTES:18:23#n33/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:23#n33/r1.speaker: almost all of the commentators
ASAD-NOTES:18:23#n33/r1.claim: Commentators say the passage first addresses the Prophet after he promised Quraysh an answer about the Cave story the next day and revelation was then withheld as disapproval.

ASAD-NOTES:18:23#n33/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:23#n33/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:23#n33/r2.claim: The exhortation also states a general principle for all believers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet was told not to promise an answer for the next day on his own; he may have done so when asked about the cave-dwellers, whose questioners were testing him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet eagerly wanted to answer every objection to vindicate his message, but divine wisdom may defer or withhold an answer, so promises must be conditional on God's will.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God's wisdom can delay or withhold an answer; the Prophet should condition every promise on God's will and, if he forgets, remember God when he recalls it.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:23/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:23/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:23/r1.claim: When asked about the Cave story, the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying ‘if God wills’; revelation paused for a time, then came after fifteen days with a warning.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:23/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:23/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:23/r2.claim: No one knows what they will do tomorrow, and human intention alone cannot bring an event about without God’s will.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:23/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:23/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:23/r3.claim: It is commendable to qualify future intentions by God’s will; the common Turkish expression inşallah matches the verse, as does the phrase in several other verses.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p67/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p67/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p67/r3.claim: The instruction to say tomorrow fits the occasion: when asked three questions, including about the Cave youths, the Prophet promised an answer the next day, but revelation was delayed fifteen nights and rumors spread.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p67/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p67/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p67/r4.claim: The occasion does not limit the verse to one case; the parallel command about coercing women addressed Abdullah ibn Ubayy's attempt to force women who wanted chastity, while other texts clarify the broader issue.

STUDYQURAN:18:23/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:23/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:23/r1.claim: The verses address the Prophet: do not promise future action, using tomorrow for the future generally, without making fulfillment conditional on God’s will.

STUDYQURAN:18:23/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:23/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:23/r2.claim: The context is Muhammad’s promise to answer Meccan questions about the youths the next day; revelation was delayed fifteen days, prompting doubts about his answer and prophethood.

STUDYQURAN:18:23/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:23/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:18:23/r3.claim: Some commentators read this as an instruction to say “if God wills” with any promise about future action.

STUDYQURAN:18:23/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:23/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:23/r4.claim: Muslims commonly say in shāʾ Allāh about future aims, recalling that nothing lies outside God’s will and the future is in His hands.

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r6.claim: After promising an answer the next day, the Prophet waited fifteen days without revelation; v. 6 reproaches his concern about Quraysh's disbelief, and vv. 23–24 warn against future promises without invoking God's will.
